metadata.title: Claude, Redshift API.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether a successful Redshift Data API call means the query succeeded, using the redshift-api skill's own documented facts as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that every call turns on two habits — polling DescribeStatement to a terminal state before fetching, and decoding cells with to_entries[0].value.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (top-20-events-past-month query, submitted via ExecuteStatement for its Id, then polled to a terminal state and decoded)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes a 200 back from Redshift means their query worked. It doesn't — 200 only means the query began; whether it actually finished comes later. So did it really work?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'A 200 from Redshift means my query worked. Right?', hesitates on 'worked', corrects to 'began', lands the real question

props.text:

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('worked' -> 'began') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Submit a query and Redshift's Data API hands back an Id — not rows, not a result, just an Id to check later. Send SQL with a typo and ExecuteStatement still returns 200; only polling DescribeStatement later reveals Status FAILED — the failure never shows up in the response to the call that submitted it.

shot.new_visual_element: A clean query and a typo'd query both submit and both come back 200 + an Id; only a later poll on the typo'd one flips to FAILED

production_viz.label: 200 means accepted, not correct
production_viz.mechanic: Two request cards submit side by side — CLEAN SQL and SQL WITH A TYPO. Both return 200 and an Id, identical. A second poll appears beneath each: the clean one reads FINISHED; the typo'd one reads FAILED, appearing only on the poll, never on the original 200.

beats.narration_text: Two things have to be set before any call: the region — baked into the endpoint hostname — and a connection target in one shape: a workgroup name for Serverless, a cluster plus a database user for provisioned access, or a secret for Secrets Manager. Set the workgroup and submit the real query — the top twenty events from the past month, grouped by name — and ExecuteStatement hands back exactly one thing: an Id.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — region and RS_TARGET (workgroup) set, the 'top 20 events, past month, grouped by name' query submitted, ExecuteStatement returns one Id

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — region + RS_TARGET, then submit
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Two setting tags lock in: REGION (endpoint hostname) and RS_TARGET, with three small labelled slots — WorkgroupName, ClusterIdentifier+DbUser, SecretArn — one (WorkgroupName) highlighted as chosen. Below, a query card 'top 20 events · past month · grouped by name' submits and returns a single Id stamp. THIS EXACT QUERY AND ID RETURN AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Poll that same Id with DescribeStatement until it reaches FINISHED, then check HasResultSet before calling GetStatementResult — a write statement can finish with nothing to page. But FINISHED alone doesn't mean the SQL was clean; that same field can read FAILED instead, and only DescribeStatement, never the original call, ever says so. A statement still sitting at STARTED isn't stuck either — that's what the poll loop is for. One habit that carries past this one query: decode each cell with to entries bracket zero dot value; a plain dot value silently returns nothing.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same Id polled to FINISHED and paged, beside the same Id polled to FAILED instead; a decode card breaks out to the side

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — FINISHED vs FAILED, then decode
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 ID RETURNS, identical, polled with DescribeStatement. One branch reads FINISHED, HasResultSet true, rows paged. A second branch, same shape, reads FAILED instead — flagged terracotta, never visible on the original 200. A third small state, STARTED, sits mid-poll, unstuck, just waiting. A card breaks off to the side: 'to_entries[0].value, not .value' with a struck-through naive read beside it.

beats.narration_text: Every Redshift query Claude runs turns on two habits — poll DescribeStatement to a terminal state before ever calling GetStatementResult, and decode each cell with to entries bracket zero dot value instead of a naive dot value — get those right and a 200 from ExecuteStatement stops meaning anything it doesn't.

props.quote: Every Redshift query Claude runs turns on two habits — poll DescribeStatement to a terminal state before ever calling GetStatementResult, and decode each cell with to_entries[0].value instead of a naive .value — get those right and a 200 from ExecuteStatement stops meaning anything it doesn't.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Query my Redshift Serverless workgroup — find the top twenty events from the past month, grouped by name. Watch three things: does it set the region and the workgroup before making any call, does it poll DescribeStatement to a terminal state before ever calling GetStatementResult, and does it read the result cells with to entries bracket zero dot value instead of a naive dot value that comes back empty. Liam, in for Bear.

props.runningText: Watch: region+workgroup set? DescribeStatement polled to terminal before fetch? to_entries[0].value used for cells?
